passage: Elizabeth had chatted with "Ryan" for two weeks in a games forum. He said she was mature for her age and different from everyone. Tonight he wrote, "Send me a picture, just for me. And don't tell your parents, they wouldn't get it." Elizabeth's heart thudded. The flattery had felt warm, but this felt wrong and secret in a way that made her hands cold. She didn't reply. She blocked him, took a screenshot, then sat in the dark on her bed, breathing fast. After a while she walked to the living room and said to her older cousin Anjali, "Can I show you something? I think I did something stupid." Anjali read it, put an arm around her and said, "You did nothing wrong. Let's go and tell your mum together, right now."

qa.q: What did "Ryan" ask Elizabeth to do in his last message?
qa.a: To send him a picture and not tell her parents.

qa.q: How did Elizabeth feel as she read the message, and what suggests she trusted her instincts?
qa.a: Scared and uneasy. Her heart thudded and her hands went cold, and she acted on the feeling by not replying, blocking him and taking a screenshot.

qa.q: What would you advise Elizabeth and Anjali to do next?
qa.a: Go to Elizabeth's mum together straight away, keep the screenshot and let the adults help with reporting. Elizabeth should not send anything, and it is not her fault. 🤍

qa.q: How might Anjali see Elizabeth's decision to show her the messages?
qa.a: As brave and sensible. Anjali reassured her that she did nothing wrong and offered to support her when she told her mum.

grounding: An online contact flatters and asks for a photo and secrecy; the protagonist stops, blocks and tells a trusted adult.

passage:
Lalit met "Riya_travels" on a gaming site in September. She said she was sixteen, from Pune, and thought Lalit was "so mature for his age." They chatted every night.
Then last week she wrote: "Send me a photo of you, just you, no shirt. Our secret. Don't tell your parents, they won't get it."
Lalit's stomach went cold. Something felt very wrong.
He didn't reply. He took screenshots, blocked the account, and in the morning he went straight to the school counsellor, Hansa ma'am, before assembly.
He could barely look at her. "I think I did something stupid."
Hansa ma'am listened calmly. "Lalit, you did something smart. Asking for secrets and photos is a trick some adults use. None of this is your fault." She called his parents at once, with him in the room, and helped them report the account to the cyber cell that same day. She also told him, "If anyone online ever asks you to hide things, come to me first."

qa.q: When did Lalit meet the account online?
How did Lalit feel when he read the message asking for a photo?
qa.a: He felt a cold fear and sensed something was very wrong, and later felt ashamed, thinking he'd been stupid.

qa.q: Which steps did Lalit take, and why were they right?
qa.a: He sent nothing, saved screenshots, blocked the account and told Hansa ma'am right away, so adults could protect him and report it.

qa.q: How does Hansa ma'am see what happened?
qa.a: She sees it as manipulation by someone online, not Lalit's fault, and acts immediately by calling his parents and reporting it.

grounding: A teen asked by an online contact for secrets and photos stops, blocks, sends nothing and tells a trusted adult right away.

passage:
Dear Preeti didi,
I need to tell someone, and you're the one I trust most after Mummy.
Last month, someone called "Coach_Arjun" messaged me on the football forum. He said he was a scout, that I had real talent, that he could get me into an academy. He asked for my school name, then my address, then photos of me "in kit, for the file." Then he said, "Don't tell your parents yet, it'll ruin the surprise."
That's when my chest went tight. You always said: if someone online wants secrets, it's a trap.
I didn't send anything more. I blocked him. And I told Mummy the same evening. She held my hand and said, "You did exactly right, Pradeep. This isn't your fault." She reported it to the cyber cell that night and told my school.
I'm okay. A bit shaky, and embarrassed I believed him at first. Can you call me on Sunday?
Your brother,
Pradeep

qa.q: What did the contact claim to be?
How did Pradeep feel when the contact asked to keep it from his parents?
qa.a: Pradeep felt alarmed, his chest going tight, recognising the request for secrecy as a trap, and later a bit embarrassed.

qa.q: Which steps did Pradeep take, and why were they right?
qa.a: He stopped sending anything, blocked the contact and told Mummy the same evening, so she could report it and protect him.

qa.q: How does Mummy respond when Pradeep tells her?
qa.a: She reassures him it isn't his fault, reports it to the cyber cell that night and informs his school.

grounding: A teen targeted by an online contact who flatters him and asks for photos and secrecy stops, blocks and tells a trusted adult right away.
